title: api: strengthen rate-limit semantics, idempotency handling, retry-after and OpenAI-compat error codes
author: Aria Patel
release_notes: Improved API robustness: standardized rate-limit headers (Retry-After semantics), consistent error codes across OpenAI-compat layer, safer idempotency handling for streaming endpoints, and clearer client-visible errors. No breaking changes expected; backward compatible headers are additive.
description:
Context: We have several customer reports and internal e2e failures around ambiguous rate-limit behavior during streaming and function-calling flows, and inconsistent error shapes between Redwood's native API and the OpenAI-compatibility layer. This caused retry logic in some SDKs to mis-handle streaming interruptions and to re-play tool calls that should have been idempotent.

Goal: Unify rate-limit semantics (including Retry-After header precision), make idempotency behavior explicit for streaming/tool-calls, and normalize error codes/shapes in the OpenAI compatibility layer so client SDKs and customer infrastructure can rely on consistent signals.

What this PR does (summary):
- Standardizes HTTP rate-limit headers across handlers: adds X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset and ensures Retry-After is present and uses seconds (int) for HTTP 429 and 503 responses.
- Adds a canonical JSON error shape for OpenAI-compat paths (error.type, error.message, error.code) and maps existing internal errors to this shape.
- Introduces idempotency key checks for streaming endpoints and function/tool-calling paths: requests with Idempotency-Key are now tracked until the server returns a terminal response (success/error) and intermediate streaming fragments are annotated with a transient "stream_sequence" value for better client replay decisions.
- Improves server-side retry hints: differentiate transient (retryable) vs permanent errors using the new error.code field.
- Updates SDK-facing behavior notes in OpenAPI/compat docs and augments tests and e2e harnesses for streaming reconnection scenarios.

Checklist:
- [x] Add/standardize headers and Retry-After semantics
- [x] Normalize error shapes for OpenAI-compat endpoints
- [x] Implement idempotency tracking for streaming/tool calls
- [x] Add integration tests for retry-after + streaming reconnects
- [x] Update docs & compatibility notes

Backwards compatibility: Changes are additive and opt-in: existing clients that don't set Idempotency-Key see unchanged semantics. The error shape change applies to OpenAI-compat endpoints only and is backward compatible for most clients since it fills in missing fields rather than removing them. SDKs should be able to parse both legacy and new shapes.

Testing: unit tests for header plumbing, integration tests that simulate throttling and verify Retry-After header and client backoff behavior, end-to-end tests reproducing the incident scenario where a streaming connection was retried and a tool call was executed twice.

Notes: This PR touches critical API surfaces (streaming, function-calls). We kept changes small and gated the idempotency store behind a short TTL (5 minutes) and a feature flag to allow fast rollback if needed.

review_comments: Diego Martinez (2026-02-11): Please add a comment on the TTL chosen for idempotency store and rationale for 5m. Also, would prefer Retry-After in seconds (not HTTP date) to make SDK backoff simpler.

Aria Patel (2026-02-11): Reply: TTL set to 5m based on tail-latency observed in incident traces; added config flag for cluster-wide override. We standardized Retry-After to seconds per request (good call).
Hannah Li (2026-02-12): Could we ensure older SDKs that expect the legacy error.message field keep seeing it? Suggest we include both legacy_message and error.message during a transition window.
Aria Patel (2026-02-12): Reply: Implemented compatibility layer in error_mapper that preserves legacy_message under legacy_message key while populating error.message. Added unit tests.
Sanjay Kumar (2026-02-13): Approve after CI green. One nit: add a short note to the deploy runbook about the feature flag for idempotency store.
Aria Patel (2026-02-13): Addressed: added runbook note and feature-flag toggle with rollback steps. CI rerun requested.
CI (2026-02-14): Integration tests passed on rerun. All checks green.

Rollback: clear feature flag if duplicate tool calls spike > 0.1% over baseline
